markdown:
**Methane Watch brief: Recurring methane, Shanxi and Ordos coal basin site** (draft `brief-20261008T194905-33e590`, not filed)

Site: Near Xinxiang, Henan, eastern Shanxi and Ordos coal basin, China (35.4451, 114.5779), watch area shanxi coal basin
Looks: EMIT looked 21 times; 5 of 8 recent passes read are candidates.

- TROPOMI 14-day composite (2026-09-22 to 2026-10-06) shows a top hotspot anomaly of +67.6 ppb above background at this location.
- EMIT looked 21 times (2023-02-27 to 2026-06-05); NASA outlined 0 plumes here in the formal product.
- 5 of 8 recent passes read since 2025-01-01 are candidates, peaking at 1,841.6 ppm·m on 2025-05-28.
- Candidates span 5 separate dates: 2025-03-31, 2025-05-28, 2025-06-22, 2026-06-01, and 2026-06-05.
- 3 passes were rejected: 1 too weak, 2 within noise.
- VIIRS saw no heat source within 1 km over the last 30 nights; flaring was not observed.
- Check: VIIRS saw no heat source within 1 km over the last 30 nights; flaring was not observed (small or brief flares can be missed).
- Check: Overture Maps shows within 2 km: 1 pipeline (0 km); nothing mapped for mining, waste, wetland.
- Check: The public registry lists within 2 km: 1 pipeline (0.2 km); no operator on record for any of them; records dated 2014.

| Hypothesis (unconfirmed) | Assessment | What would confirm or rule it out |
|---|---|---|
| Routine venting | possible | Repeated candidates on 5 separate dates support recurrence; a ground inspection or aircraft survey would confirm continuous venting. |
| Equipment failure or leak | possible | Persistent multi-date signal without NASA plume outlines; a follow-up EMIT pass or aircraft survey would distinguish a leak from routine venting. |
| Unlit or malfunctioning flare | cannot assess | No heat detected by VIIRS and no flare stack mapped; a night-time VIIRS survey or ground visit would confirm or rule this out. |
| Non-oil-and-gas source (landfill, coal, agriculture) | less likely | Only a pipeline is mapped within 2 km; no mining or waste facilities in Overture Maps, though mapping gaps in this coal basin are possible. |

Confidence that methane recurs at this site: high. Confidence in any single explanation: low without a ground or aircraft check.
Gaps: NASA's plume product is nearly empty after 2024, so no formal plume outlines exist for the 5 candidate passes.; EMIT only sees the site on its passes; gaps between passes leave emissions unobserved.; Overture Maps and the public registry may have mapping gaps in this coal basin region.; TROPOMI at ~4 km resolution cannot resolve individual sources within the hotspot..
Next collection: A targeted EMIT pass or airborne survey over this site to confirm recurrence and estimate flux.

Status: DRAFT, awaiting the analyst's decision.
